assistant.welcome:
Hello and welcome! This is the Shaveh BeShaveh digital assistant — an AI-based system, not a human representative. You can ask any question about using the app, the plans and the shared account.
To cancel a transaction, request a refund, or make a privacy or accessibility request — you can contact us directly at any time: via “Contact a representative”, by email at shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com, or with the cancellation form in the app (the “Cancel a transaction” link at the bottom of the home screen).

articles.title: What is Shaveh BeShaveh?
articles.summary: Shaveh BeShaveh is a web app for splitting expenses and settling up in a group: open a group, friends join with a link, record who paid — and the app works out who owes whom.
articles.body:
Shaveh BeShaveh is a web app for splitting shared expenses — for a trip, a barbecue, a family get-together, a team night out, a celebration, an event production, a renovation project or a shared apartment.
Here's how it works:
1. Open a group for the occasion.
2. Friends join with a link — no installation and no sign-up, just a name and a phone number.
3. Whoever pays records the expense: the amount, who paid, and who it's split between. You can attach a photo of the receipt.
4. The app calculates how much each person paid, what their share is, and how much they still need to get back or pay — and shows “Who pays whom”.
Good to know: the app only calculates and displays. No money passes through it — transfers are made directly between you (bank transfer, payment app, cash and so on), and recording a payment (“I paid” / “I received”) is just a record.

articles.title: Getting started: opening your first group
articles.summary: Open your first group in four steps: choose what you're organizing, enter your name and phone number, accept the Terms — and send friends an invite link.
articles.body:
1. On the home screen, choose “What are you organizing?” — a trip, a barbecue, a family get-together and so on (or “New group” if you already have groups).
2. Enter a name for the group, plus your own name and phone number. You're automatically added as the first participant and as the group's organizer.
3. Optional: location, icon, dates, the group's base currency, budget, organizer password, and how expenses are split.
4. Accept the Terms and save — your group is open.
5. Send friends an invite link (the “Invite” button in the bar under the group name, or “Invite friends” on a new group's welcome card), and they join on their own.
You can also add participants by name in the group settings, but the invite link is the easiest way.

articles.title: Quick split — no group, no sign-up
articles.summary: “Quick split” on the home screen: type an amount and how many people — and instantly see “X each”. Send it to WhatsApp as text or as an image, without opening a group. Saved on your device only.
articles.body:
When you just need to split one bill — say a meal or a taxi — you don't have to open a group:
1. On the home screen, tap “Quick split” (below the “What are you organizing?” heading and above the group types, or below your list of groups).
2. Type the total amount in shekels (you can also type a calculation, e.g. 120+35), and use the “How many people?” counter to choose between 2 and 30.
3. “Rounding” (optional): “No rounding”, “To ₪1”, “To ₪5” or “To ₪10” — with rounding, each person's amount is a round number, and the “Rounding total” is shown above the bill. Without rounding, if there's a few agorot left over, the app shows which amounts include it.
4. “Names (optional)” — you can enter names; they only appear in the text and image you share.
The result — “₪X each” — appears instantly. “Send to the WhatsApp group” opens a ready-made message; “Share as image” creates a designed card; “Copy” copies the text.
“Turn into a real group” opens a regular group with the amount added as its first expense — so you can keep recording the rest of that occasion's expenses.
Privacy: the quick split is saved on your device only (a single draft, deleted with “Clear”) — nothing is sent to the server, and no phone number or sign-up is needed.

articles.title: What kinds of groups can I open?
articles.summary: Trip, barbecue, family get-together, team night out, wedding, event production, contractor or shared apartment — what the type changes, and what stays the same in every group.
articles.body:
When you open a group, you choose a type. The type sets the list of categories suggested for expenses, the icon and the wording of messages — but everything works the same in every type:
• Trip
• Family get-together
• Barbecue / cookout
• Team night out / team building
• Class reunion
• Wedding / celebration
• Event production
• Contractor / project
• Shared apartment
• Something else
Barbecue and family get-together groups start out split “Per head” (adults and children), since families usually come together. All other types start out “Equal per participant”. You can change this anytime in the group settings.

articles.title: Trip group
articles.summary: A group for a trip at home or abroad: destination and dates, tailored categories, a currency converter, and foreign-currency expenses calculated in the group's currency.
articles.body:
A trip group suits travel at home or abroad.
What's special about it:
• You can set a destination and dates. In the web version, a photo of the destination sometimes appears on the group card and in the invite.
• Suggested categories: food & restaurants, accommodation, transport, flights, shopping, activities & attractions, groceries, and other.
• A currency converter appears at the top of the group, so you can quickly check what something costs in the local currency.
• You can record each expense in the currency it was paid in; balances are calculated in the group's base currency.
• With dates and a budget, you also get a daily budget (“Left for today”), accommodation spread over several nights, and an end-of-trip forecast — see “Daily budget, spreading over days and future expenses”.
• At the end of the trip: “Share a keepsake” also offers a “Boarding pass” and a “Passport” — designed images for Stories and WhatsApp; and the destinations from all your trip groups are collected in “My countries” on the home screen.
Tip: for a trip of several days, the “Week” or “Month” plan usually fits, depending on how many expenses you expect.

articles.title: “My countries” — destination stamps from your trip groups
articles.summary: “My countries” on the home screen shows the destinations from your trip groups as passport stamps: a flag when the destination is recognized, the destination name and the year you visited — no points and no rankings.
articles.body:
When you have trip groups with a destination, the home screen shows “My countries” below your list of groups: a passport stamp for each destination, with its flag (when the destination is recognized — e.g. “Hungary” or “Prague”), the destination name as you wrote it, the years you visited, and the number of groups for that destination.
How it works:
• The destination comes from the “Destination” field of a trip group — so it's worth writing a clear name (a country or a city).
• Two destinations with the same name merge into one stamp; “Trip to Hungary” and “Hungary” are counted together.
• Archived groups count too — the memories stay.
• The data stays on your device: it's a personal view of the groups you're a member of, not a score or a competition.
In a trip group, “Share a keepsake” also offers the “Passport” card — the group's destination stamp alongside small stamps of your other destinations.

articles.title: Barbecue and family get-together
articles.summary: Barbecues and family get-togethers are split “Per head”: each family is one account with a number of adults and children, and the organizer decides how much is paid per child.
articles.body:
Barbecues and family get-togethers are usually attended by families, so the group opens with a “Per head” split:
• Each participant is one account (for example, a family), with a number of adults and a number of children.
• The group organizer decides how much is paid per child: free, a quarter, half (the default), three quarters, or full price.
• Barbecue categories: meat & fish, groceries, drinks, equipment, transport, activities and other. Family get-together: food, groceries, hosting, gifts and more.
For a barbecue or a small shared meal, the free plan is usually enough.

articles.title: Team night out, class reunion and wedding / celebration
articles.summary: Team night out, class reunion, wedding or celebration: fitting categories (venue, catering, music, photography) plus budget and visibility options for people funding something together.
articles.body:
These types suit occasions where several people fund something together: a team night out or team-building day, a class reunion, and a wedding, Sheva Brachot or family celebration.
• Suggested categories include, among others: venue & location, catering, music & band, photography, decor & flowers, gifts and drinks.
• You can set a budget and track how much has been used with the progress bar. If you go over, an alert is shown.
• “What participants see”: the group organizer decides whether everyone sees all expenses and everyone's balance, or each person sees only their own.

articles.title: Event production and contractor / project
articles.summary: Event production and contractor / project — managing expenses for a client or partners: professional categories, a business license and branding with your business logo.
articles.body:
“Event production” and “Contractor / project” are for people who manage expenses on behalf of a client or partners — producers, contractors and organizers.
• Production: venue & location, catering, music, photography, decor, staff, moving & delivery, and other.
• Contractor / project: materials, workers, tools & rental, moving & delivery, bills, and other.
• The group works exactly like any other group: who paid, who it's split between, and who pays whom.
If you open many groups, there's a business license (monthly or yearly): unlimited groups and expenses, with your business logo and name on invites and messages.

articles.title: Shared apartment
articles.summary: Shared apartment: rent, bills, groceries and cleaning in one ongoing group, with the yearly plan for unlimited expenses and a record of every transfer.
articles.body:
A “Shared apartment” group suits recurring expenses: rent, bills, groceries, cleaning, food and supplies.
Good to know:
• It's an ongoing group, so expenses build up over time. The “Yearly” plan (₪250 a year, unlimited expenses) is made exactly for this.
• After each transfer between roommates, record it with the “I paid” (or “I received”) button, and the balance resets accordingly.
• If a roommate leaves and a new one moves in — the new roommate joins with the link and chooses “From now on only”, so they don't share in expenses from before they arrived.

articles.title: Group settings: what you can change
articles.summary: What you can change in the group settings: name, icon and dates, currency and rates, budget, notifications, split method, organizer password and what participants see.
articles.body:
Open the settings with the gear button at the top of the group. It's shown to the group organizer only.
What you can change:
• Name, location, icon and dates.
• The base currency and exchange rates (including “Update to today's live rate” in the web version).
• Budget, plus sound and notifications for new expenses.
• Organizer password, and what participants see.
• How expenses are split (equal per participant / per head) and how much is paid per child.
• How you settle up at the end (direct / netting).
• Participants: add by name, and remove anyone who isn't yet on any expense.
When you're done, tap “Save”. Deleting the group is also at the bottom of the settings.

articles.title: What can the group organizer do?
articles.summary: The group organizer sees all expenses and the group overview, changes settings, deletes expenses, closes the books and activates plans — exactly what they're allowed to do.
articles.body:
Whoever opens the group is its organizer. The organizer has a few extra abilities:
• Sees all expenses and the “Group overview” — every participant's balance.
• Changes the group settings and decides what participants see.
• Deletes expenses directly, and approves or rejects participants' deletion requests.
• Switches between participants' accounts — for example, to record on behalf of someone without a smartphone.
• Retroactively adds a participant to expenses recorded before they joined.
• Closes the group for final settlement and sends each person who owes a personal message.
• Chooses a plan, and can split its cost between participants.
To manage the group from several devices, set an organizer password in the settings. When handing the role over to another participant, they open organizer access on their own device by signing in with the organizer password.

articles.title: What do participants see? (privacy within the group)
articles.summary: Three privacy switches within the group: which expenses participants see, whether they see everyone's balance, and which summary they're shown.
articles.body:
The group organizer sets three switches in the settings. The organizer always sees everything.
1. Expenses: all of the group's expenses, or only the expenses the participant is part of.
2. Balance: every participant's balance, or only their personal account.
3. Summary: the full group summary, or a personal summary only.
The default is full privacy — each participant sees only their own. The “Who actually paid” breakdown in the summary is always visible to the organizer only.
Please note: anyone with the invite link can reach the group's data, so send it only to group members.

articles.title: Organizer password: managing the group from several devices
articles.summary: An organizer password lets you manage the group from a new phone, a computer or another organizer's device — how to set it and how to sign in with it.
articles.body:
An organizer password lets you manage the group from another device too — a new phone, a computer, or another organizer's device.
How to set it:
1. Open the group settings.
2. Fill in “Group organizer password” and save. To change the password, enter a new one; leave it empty if nothing changes.
How to sign in from another device:
1. Open the group's invite link.
2. Tap “Group organizer? Sign in with the organizer password” — on the join screen or on the “Who are you in the group?” screen — enter the password and tap “Open group management”. This option only appears once a password has been set.
3. If you've already signed in on this device with the organizer's name and phone number — the top of the group screen shows “Management isn't open on this device yet”, with a “Sign in with password” button.
Signing in with name and phone number alone doesn't open management: the organizer's phone number is visible to anyone who sends them money, so management opens only on the device that created the group or after signing in with the password.
Choose a password you don't use anywhere else, and don't share it in the WhatsApp group.

articles.title: Inviting friends to the group
articles.summary: Inviting friends to the group: the “Invite” button, sending on WhatsApp with a ready-made message, copying the link — and friends join on their own, no installation needed.
articles.body:
1. Inside the group, tap “Invite” in the bar under the group name (in a new group — also “Invite friends” on the welcome card). The “Invite friends” window opens.
2. Choose: “Send on WhatsApp” — opens a ready-made invite message with the link; “Send as image” — a designed invite card (the group's icon and name, who's already in, “Join in one tap — free, no installation”) sent as an image, with the link included only in the message text (the image has no link); “Copy link”; or “Other ways to share…”.
3. Whoever gets the link opens it, enters a name and phone number — and joins right away.
There's nothing to install and no sign-up.
Important: the link gives access to the group's data. Send it only to group members — for example, in the occasion's WhatsApp group.

articles.title: How do I join a group from a link?
articles.summary: How to join a group from an invite link: tap the link, enter your name and phone number, choose “From now on only” or “Also what's already been paid” — and you're in.
articles.body:
1. Tap the link you received. The “You're invited to join…” screen opens with the group name and the participants already in it.
2. Enter your name and phone number in international format, with + and the country code (e.g. +44 7911 123456). The number identifies you in the group — including when you sign in from another device. It's visible to group members (anyone with the invite link), and is never sold or passed on for marketing.
3. In a group split per head — say how many adults and how many children are coming with you.
4. If expenses have already been recorded in the group — choose “From now on only” or “Also what's already been paid”.
5. Tap “Join the group” (which also means you accept the Terms).
Already registered, or did the organizer add you in advance by name? Enter the same name and phone number — and the app recognizes you. Typed a slightly different name (e.g. “David Cohen” when the organizer entered “David”)? You'll be asked “Are you David?” — “Yes, that's me” links you to the existing account, with the expenses already recorded on it, and “No, that's not me” opens a new account. You can also tap “Already registered? Choose your name” at the bottom of the screen and pick your name from the list.

articles.title: Joining midway: “From now on only” or “Also what's already been paid”
articles.summary: Joining when there are already expenses? Choose “From now on only” (earlier expenses don't change) or “Also what's already been paid” (everyone's balance is updated).
articles.body:
Anyone joining a group that already has expenses chooses:
• “From now on only” — you share only in expenses recorded from the moment you join. Earlier expenses don't change.
• “Also what's already been paid” — you also join the shared expenses already recorded, and everyone's balance is updated.
What “Also what's already been paid” includes: only expenses split across the whole group. Not included: a private expense, an expense shared by only some members, an expense with manual amounts, percentages, shares or by items, and payment records (“I paid” / “I received”).
In a group that's been closed for settlement, you can only join from now on.
If some earlier expenses weren't added (for example, because of a network error), a message appears, and the group organizer can complete this from the participant's card.

articles.title: The organizer adds participants or adds them retroactively
articles.summary: The group organizer adds participants by name from the group settings, and decides whether they share from now on only or also in expenses already recorded.
articles.body:
The group organizer can add participants themselves:
1. In the group settings, under “Participants in the group”, type a name and tap “Add”.
2. If expenses have already been recorded, choose whether the new participants share “From now on only” or “Also what's already been paid”.
3. Save.
A participant added by name can later join with the link using the same name and their phone number, and the account will be linked to them.
Adding an existing participant retroactively: in the “Group overview”, tap the participant. If they joined “From now on only” and there are earlier shared expenses, an “Also add to expenses already recorded” button appears.
Recorded expenses before your friends joined? When you're the only one in the group, “Everyone” is just you — and the expense stays on you. When someone joins later “From now on only”, the group screen shows an “Expenses recorded before friends joined” message, with an “Add” button for each new member (with confirmation) or “Leave as is”.

articles.title: Signing in to my account and “Who are you in the group?”
articles.summary: On a new device or after clearing your browser: choose your name from the list, verify with the phone number you joined with — and your personal account is back.
articles.body:
On each device, the app remembers who you are in each group. On a new device, or after clearing your browser data, you need to sign in again:
1. Open the group (or the invite link).
2. Choose your name from the list.
3. Enter the phone number you joined with and tap “Sign in to account”.
Anyone entering a number registered to a different name is asked “Is this you?” before the account opens.
• “The phone number doesn't match the selected name” — check that it's the number you joined with.
• “No phone number has been registered for this participant yet” — contact the group organizer.
• Not on the list? “Join as a new participant”.

articles.title: Adding an expense
articles.summary: Adding an expense: amount and currency, category, who paid and who it's split between, date and description, and a receipt photo — plus what happens after you save.
articles.body:
1. Inside the group, tap “New expense”.
2. Enter the amount and choose a currency (if it differs from the group's currency — confirm or update the exchange rate).
3. Choose a category.
4. “Who paid?” — whoever actually paid.
5. “Split between?” — select the people the expense belongs to (default: everyone).
6. “How is it split?” — equally, per head, manual amounts, percentages, shares or by items (for a restaurant: each item and who shares it).
7. Optional: date, a short description and a receipt photo.
8. Tap “Save expense” — and balances update for everyone.
Shortcut: when your previous expense differed from the default (e.g. a different category, a different currency or only some of the participants), a “Same as last time” chip appears above the categories — one tap fills in all of that, and tapping again restores the default. On a trip abroad, if your previous expense was recorded in a foreign currency within the last two days, the currency already opens that way (“Same as last time (EUR) — you can change it”). The category and the split never change on their own.
If you see “The group has reached the plan's expense limit”, the group organizer can choose a plan or a top-up.

articles.title: Editing an expense
articles.summary: Editing a recorded expense: who can edit it (whoever recorded it and the group organizer), what you can change, and how balances update.
articles.body:
1. Tap the expense in the list (“My expenses” or “All group expenses”).
2. Change whatever you need — amount, currency, who paid, who it's split between, split method, date, description or receipt.
3. Tap “Save changes”.
Made a mistake? Right after saving, “Expense updated ✓” appears with an “Undo” button — tapping it within 10 seconds restores the expense to how it was (as long as the receipt wasn't replaced).
Who can edit: whoever recorded the expense, and the group organizer. Other participants can only view the expense details, and can ask the organizer to delete it.
Every change immediately updates the balances and “Who pays whom” for all participants. If the expense was already settled with a recorded payment (“I paid” / “I received”), correcting the amount may create a small new balance — that's fine: it shows up in “Who owes whom” and is settled like any other debt.

articles.title: Searching expenses
articles.summary: In a group with lots of expenses: a search field above the list — by description, category, who paid, participant, amount or date; combined with the category and payer filters.
articles.body:
When the “Whole group” list has 8 or more expenses, a “Search expenses” field appears above the filter chips.
1. Type a word — a description (“taxi”), a category name (“accommodation”), who paid, who's in the split, a date (“September”) or an amount (“96” finds 96, 96.5 and also 960 — any amount starting with 96).
2. The list updates as you type, and the line “Showing: N expenses · Total…” sums up the results. With several words — all of them must appear.
3. “Clear” (or Esc) deletes the search; “All” in the filter chips clears it too.
Search works together with the category and payer filters, isn't saved and isn't sent anywhere. In a group where each participant sees only their own expenses — other people's expenses can be found only by amount and payer name.

articles.title: Deleting an expense and deletion requests
articles.summary: Deleting an expense: whoever recorded it and the organizer delete it directly (with “Undo” for 10 seconds); other participants send a deletion request for the organizer to approve.
articles.body:
Deleting an expense depends on your role:
• Whoever recorded the expense, and the group organizer, delete it directly: open the expense, tap “Delete expense” and confirm. For about 10 seconds an “Undo” button appears that brings the expense back.
• Other participants in the expense send a request: open the expense, tap “Ask the organizer to delete” and “Send request”. The expense stays, marked ⏳, until the organizer decides.
The organizer sees “Deletion requests awaiting your approval”. Open the expense and choose “Approve and delete” or “Reject request”. If rejected, the expense stays as it was.
A payment record between participants (“I paid” / “I received”) is deleted from the “Recorded payments” list. Whoever recorded it and the organizer can do this.

articles.title: Categories and budget
articles.summary: Categories tailored to the group type with a breakdown in the summary, and a group budget with a progress bar and an alert as you get close to it.
articles.body:
Categories: for each expense, choose a category from a list tailored to the group type. Categories already used in the group are always shown. The group summary shows a breakdown by category. The group organizer can add their own categories — “Manage categories” at the end of the category grid in the expense form (see “Custom group categories”).
Budget:
1. In the group settings, fill in “Budget” in the group's base currency.
2. The group page shows a meter: how much of the budget has been used, as a percentage, and how much is left.
3. If you go over, an alert shows the amount you're over by.
The budget meter is shown to the organizer, and to participants only when the organizer has opened the group summary to them.
Daily budget: below the meter you can also set a budget per day (“Set a daily budget”) and see “Left for today” — details in the article “Daily budget, spreading over days and future expenses”.

articles.title: Daily budget, spreading over days and future expenses
articles.summary: A daily budget with “Left for today” on the status card, spreading an expense over several days, a “Future” tag, plus a breakdown by period, a heat map and a forecast in the summary.
articles.body:
Daily budget: the group organizer taps “Set a daily budget” on the “Your status” card and chooses — “Based on the overall budget” (the budget divided by the group's days) or “Fixed amount per day”. Save with the “Save daily budget” button; to edit — “Edit daily budget”.
“Left for today”: while the group is active (within its dates, or always if it has no dates), the status card shows how much of the daily budget is left after today's expenses. Once it's over, the daily budget is shown against the actual average. The organizer sees it, and so do participants — when the group summary is open to them.
Spreading over days: in the expense form, use the “How many days does this expense cover?” counter — for example, 3 for three nights' accommodation. The amount is spread in equal parts from the expense date onward — only in the daily average, the heat map and the forecast. The split between participants and the balances don't change.
Future expense: an expense dated later than today is tagged “Future” in the list and counts in the daily statistics only from its date. In the split and the balances it counts right away, like any expense — so “Who owes whom” also includes what's already been booked.
In the full summary: “By period” — a breakdown by category with a Today / This week / This month / Whole group filter — expenses already recorded for upcoming days are included in the breakdown, and the summary line notes “of which … future”; “Pace vs. budget” — today, daily average and daily budget; “Spending days” — a monthly heat map (darker = a more expensive day, future days marked with a dashed outline); and “Forecast to the group's end” — when there are dates, where you'll end up at the current pace compared with the budget.
Accessibility: every chart and map has a text description — “Text description of the map” below the heat map, and the data itself is read out to screen readers.

articles.title: Receipt photos and the receipt gallery
articles.summary: A receipt photo for every expense: take a picture or choose from your gallery, the image is resized automatically, “Read from receipt” fills in the form, and all receipts are collected in a gallery in the summary.
articles.body:
You can attach a photo of the receipt to any expense:
1. In the expense form, tap the “Receipt” box.
2. Take a photo, or choose an image from your gallery.
3. Save the expense.
The image is resized automatically to save space. To replace or remove it — open the expense and tap “Remove ✕” on the image.
Read from receipt: when the digital assistant is active, a “Read from receipt” button appears below a newly attached image. Tapping it sends the image for automatic reading (AI), and the amount, currency, date and description fill in the form. Nothing is saved until you tap “Save expense” — check the details first. If items were read too, “Split by the items read” appears, for splitting by what each participant ordered. The image is sent only when you tap; the AI provider (Anthropic) keeps it for a limited time only, under its commercial terms (security and abuse prevention), and it isn't used to train models — details in the Privacy Policy.
All of the group's receipts are collected under “Receipts” in the full summary. Tap a receipt to enlarge it.
Please note: anyone who can see the expense can also see its receipt. Before taking the photo, it's a good idea to cover sensitive details, such as credit card digits.

articles.title: Equal split and choosing who's in the expense
articles.summary: The default: the expense is split equally between the people selected under “Split between?” — a meal for everyone, a taxi for three, or a private purchase.
articles.body:
The default: the expense is split equally between all participants selected under “Split between?”.
Examples:
• A meal for the whole group — leave everyone selected.
• A taxi for three — select only those three.
• A private purchase someone else paid for — select only the person the expense belongs to.
The person who paid doesn't have to be among the participants in the expense. If they paid only for others, the full amount is credited to them.
In a group split “Per head”, “Equally” is calculated by the number of people. You can choose “Equal per participant” for a specific expense only.

articles.title: Unequal split: manual amounts, percentages or shares
articles.summary: Unequal split: “Manual amounts” for each participant, “Percentages” (totaling 100%) or “Shares” (e.g. 2 shares for a couple) — with a live preview of each person's amount.
articles.body:
When each participant had something different and you know how much each person owes (for a meal where everyone ordered a dish — splitting “By items” is easier):
1. In the expense form, enter the total amount.
2. Under “How is it split?”, choose “Manual amounts”.
3. Enter each participant's amount.
4. The message below the list helps you balance it: “Left to allocate…”, “Over-allocated…”, or “The split is balanced ✓”.
5. Save. A manual split can't be saved unless it balances exactly.
“Percentages” — when you've agreed on a proportion in advance (e.g. 60/40 between two partners): enter each participant's percentage. Each person's resulting amount is shown right next to their name, and the message below the list shows “X% left to allocate” or “Total: 100% ✓”. You can save only when the total is 100.
“Shares” — when splitting by simple weights: the split is proportional to shares — for example, 2 shares for a couple and 1 share for someone coming alone, or 3 shares for whoever sleeps in the big room. Increase or decrease each participant's shares with the + and − buttons, and each participant's amount updates instantly. 0 shares — no part in this expense.
In a group split per head, a split by percentages or shares sets each account's part in this expense only — the number of adults and children doesn't affect it.
Please note: an expense with manual amounts, percentages or shares isn't updated automatically when someone joins with “Also what's already been paid”. If it needs changing, edit it manually.

articles.title: By items — splitting a restaurant bill
articles.summary: Splitting by items: enter each item from the bill — name, amount and who shares it — and the app calculates each participant's part; whatever's left (tip or service) is split equally among everyone.
articles.body:
Ideal for a restaurant bill where each participant ordered something different:
1. In the expense form, enter the bill's total amount (including tip or service).
2. Under “How is it split?”, choose “By items”.
3. For each item, enter a name (optional) and an amount, and select who shares it — “Everyone” or specific participants. “Add item” adds a row; ✕ removes it.
4. The line below the list shows the items total and the remainder — the difference between the expense amount and the items total (tip, service, rounding). The remainder is split equally among all participants in the expense.
5. “Comes to per participant” shows each participant's final amount, even before saving.
6. Save. You can't save when the items total is higher than the expense amount, when an item has no amount, or when an item has no participants.
A participant who isn't selected on any item gets only their part of the remainder. So that they pay nothing — remove them from “Split between?”.
Please note: like “Manual amounts”, an expense split by items isn't updated automatically when someone joins with “Also what's already been paid”, and only whoever recorded it (or the group organizer) can change the items.
In a group where each participant sees only their own expenses, anyone not in the expense sees the amounts used for the balance — without the item names.

articles.title: Per-head split: adults and children
articles.summary: Per-head split: each participant is an account with a number of adults and children, and the group organizer decides how much is paid per child — free, a quarter, half or full.
articles.body:
In a per-head split, each participant is one account — for example, a family — with a number of adults and children.
How to turn it on:
1. In the group settings, under “How are expenses split?”, choose “Per head — adults and children”.
2. Under “How much is paid per child?”, choose: free, quarter price, half price, three quarters, or full price.
3. Update how many adults and children are in each participant's account.
The calculation: each adult counts as 1, and each child according to the rate. A family of 2 adults and 2 children at half price counts as 3.
Switching to a per-head split also applies to expenses already recorded with an equal split. For a specific expense, you can choose “Equal per participant”.

articles.title: Updating the number of people in an account
articles.summary: In a group split per head, you can update the number of adults and children in your account at any time — when the change applies, and what the organizer can update.
articles.body:
In a group split per head, the top of your account shows the line “In your account: …”.
1. Tap “Update” on that line.
2. Change the number of adults and the number of children with the + and − buttons.
3. Save.
The group organizer can update the number of people for any participant — from the participant's card or from the group settings.
Please note: the change affects how per-head expenses are split, so everyone's balances may change. It's best to update as early as possible, and make sure everyone knows about the change.

articles.title: Foreign-currency expenses and exchange rates
articles.summary: Foreign-currency expenses: choose the currency you paid in, confirm or update the exchange rate, and balances are calculated in the group's base currency.
articles.body:
Every group has a “Base currency”, in which all balances are calculated.
An expense in another currency:
1. In the expense form, choose the currency you paid in.
2. An estimated exchange rate appears. Update it to match the actual charge on your card, if needed.
3. Save.
Good to know: there's one rate per currency in the group. Changing the rate affects all expenses in that currency.
Automatic update: by default, rates update themselves once a day to that day's rate (in the web version), and all balances are calculated using the latest rate. The group organizer can turn this off in the group settings, with the “Update rates automatically every day” switch — rates then change only when updated manually. The date of the last update appears below the rates in the settings and in the full summary.
Manually updating to today's rate: in the group settings, under “Exchange rates”, tap “Update to today's live rate” and then “Save changes”. This option is available in the web version.
You choose the base currency in the group settings. A currency that has expenses can't be removed.

articles.title: The currency converter
articles.summary: The currency converter at the top of the group: choose a currency, type an amount and instantly see what it is in the group's currency — using the rates the group uses.
articles.body:
The currency converter helps you quickly check what something costs in the group's currency. It's shown at the top of a trip group, or in any group that has a foreign currency.
1. Tap the calculator icon at the top of the group.
2. Choose the currency and type an amount. The result appears instantly.
3. ⇅ reverses the direction of the conversion.
4. “Record as expense” opens a new expense form with the amount and currency.
The calculation uses the rate saved in the group. If there isn't one — a current or estimated rate, and the rate line below the converter says so.

articles.title: Your personal account: what the numbers mean
articles.summary: The “Your status” card: you're owed money back or you still need to pay, “My share” and “I actually paid” — what each number in your personal account means.
articles.body:
When you enter a group, the “Your status” card is shown:
• The big number — “You're owed” or “You still need to pay” (or “You're all square”). That's the bottom line.
• “My share” — your share of all the expenses you're part of.
• “I actually paid” — how much you paid out of pocket.
• If a budget has been set — a thin bar at the bottom of the card shows how much of it has been used and how much is left.
Before the first expense, the card is compact, with no numbers.
Below the card:
• “Who owes whom” — the transfers you still have. Next to a transfer you need to pay there's an “I paid” button, and next to a transfer owed to you — “I received”.
• From 3 expenses on, a single tip sometimes appears — for example, how much to pay on the next expense to even out.
• “My expenses” — each expense with your share of it. Anyone allowed to see all expenses can switch between “Mine” and “Whole group”.
• “Recorded payments” — transfers already recorded.
The group organizer also sees the “Group overview” — each participant's balance.

articles.title: “Who owes whom” — how the transfers are calculated
articles.summary: “Who owes whom”: the app calculates how much each participant paid and what their share is, and shows the transfers — directly to whoever paid, or netted with the fewest transfers.
articles.body:
The app calculates how much each participant paid and what their share of the expenses is. Anyone who paid more than their share should get money back, and anyone who paid less should transfer.
The transfers themselves are shown using one of two methods, as chosen by the group organizer:
• “Directly to whoever paid” (the default) — each debt goes directly to whoever paid for it. The most transparent.
• “Netting — fewest transfers” — debts cancel each other out, and the number of transfers is as small as possible.
With both methods, each participant's balance is the same. Only the route to zero changes.
The same transfers are shown everywhere — on the group screen, in your personal account, on the closing screen and in WhatsApp messages — so everyone sees the same picture.

articles.title: Direct or netting: which settle-up method should I choose?
articles.summary: Direct or netting? In one example: paying back exactly whoever paid for you, versus fewer transfers for the whole group — and which method suits you.
articles.body:
Example: Dana paid for Noam, and Noam paid for Yoav.
• “Directly to whoever paid”: Yoav transfers to Noam, and Noam transfers to Dana. Everyone pays back exactly whoever paid for them.
• “Netting”: Yoav transfers directly to Dana, and Noam doesn't need to transfer at all, if the amounts cancel out. Fewer transfers.
Where to choose:
1. In the group settings — “How do you settle up at the end?”.
2. Or on the closing screen — which also shows the number of transfers with each method.
The choice is saved for the group and applies to all participants. In a large group, netting usually saves many transfers. In a group where it matters to everyone to see exactly who they're paying back, the direct method is clearer.

articles.title: Recording a payment: “I paid”, “I received” and partial payments
articles.summary: After you've sent or received money: “I paid” / “I received” next to the transfer, a partial payment or half, and what happens to the remaining debt.
articles.body:
After you've sent money (or received it):
1. In “Who owes whom”, tap “I paid” next to the transfer (when you sent it) or “I received” (when the money reached you).
2. In the “Record payment” window, the full amount is already filled in. For a partial payment, change the amount, or choose “Half”. The rest stays open.
3. Tap “Confirm payment”.
The payment is recorded, balances update for everyone, and it appears under “Recorded payments”.
• Whoever received the money can also record the payment — with the “I received” button.
• If the amount is higher than the open debt, you'll be asked to confirm.
• Made a mistake? Right after recording, “Payment recorded ✓” appears with an “Undo” button — tapping it within 10 seconds deletes the record and the debt returns to “Who owes whom”. After that, delete the record from “Recorded payments” (the payer or the organizer).
Important: recording a payment is just a record. It doesn't transfer money and isn't proof of a transfer.

articles.title: The group's full summary
articles.summary: The group's full summary: total expenses, daily pace, breakdown by category and period, heat map, forecast, who actually paid and the receipt gallery — and who can see it.
articles.body:
Open the summary from the “Group's full summary” row at the bottom of the group page.
What's in it:
• Total expenses and key figures.
• “Daily pace” — a chart of expenses by day (an expense spread over several days appears on each of them; future days are marked).
• “By period” — a breakdown by category with a Today / This week / This month / Whole group filter.
• “Pace vs. budget”, “Spending days” (a monthly heat map) and “Forecast to the group's end” — when there are dates.
• Breakdown by category.
• “Who actually paid” — organizer only.
• “Receipts” — all of the group's receipt photos.
Who can see it: the organizer, always. Participants — only if the organizer has opened the group summary to them in the settings. Otherwise each participant sees a personal summary.
You can send the group a summary on WhatsApp from the closing screen (“Send the full summary to the group”).

articles.title: Share a keepsake — a designed image of the group
articles.summary: “Share a keepsake” creates a designed image of the group — the classic card, the receipt, the boarding pass and the passport — for Stories and WhatsApp, with no phone numbers and no bank details.
articles.body:
At the bottom of the group screen, in the “Summary and sharing” area, you'll find “Share a keepsake” — a designed image of the group you can send on WhatsApp, post to your Story or save to your photos. The same entry also appears in the “Full summary” sheet and in the final summary after the group is closed.
The cards:
• “The classic card” — the total, number of days, expenses, participants, top categories and who paid.
• “The receipt” — the expenses line by line, like a paper receipt.
• “Boarding pass” and “Passport” — for trip groups only: the destination, the dates and a visit stamp. The “Passport” also shows small stamps of the destinations from your other trip groups on this device (as in “My countries”).
Choose a card, choose a format — “Story” (portrait, 1080×1920) or “Square” (1080×1080) — and see a preview. “Share image” opens your phone's share sheet with the image file; in a browser that doesn't support file sharing, “Save image” downloads the file so you can attach it in WhatsApp manually. “Send summary on WhatsApp” sends the summary as text.
What the image shows: the organizer (or everyone, when the summary is open to the whole group) sees the whole group; a participant sees only their own part. The image has no phone numbers and no bank details — only names, amounts and categories. The website address appears at the bottom of every card, so whoever sees the image can discover Shaveh BeShaveh.
Accessibility: below the preview there's a “Text description of the card” — everything in the image, as text.

articles.title: Closing the group and final settlement
articles.summary: Closing the group and final settlement: choose direct or netting, get a WhatsApp summary message for each participant, and the group moves to the archive.
articles.body:
At the end of the occasion, the group organizer closes the books:
1. At the bottom of the group page, in the list after “Recorded payments”, tap “Close and settle up” (this row appears for the organizer once an expense has been recorded).
2. Choose “How do you settle up?” — direct or netting. The number of transfers is shown next to each method.
3. For everyone who still needs to pay, a “Send to…” button appears: a personal WhatsApp message, straight to their number, with the amount and who to transfer to.
4. Optional: “Send the full summary to the group”.
5. “Close the group and move to archive”, and confirm.
You can close even when debts are still open. They stay recorded, and you can keep recording payments (“I paid” / “I received”). After closing, the “Final summary” opens, and it stays available to the organizer from within the group.

articles.title: Closed groups and the archive
articles.summary: A closed group in the archive: what you can still view and record, how the organizer reopens it, and when the data is deleted.
articles.body:
A closed group moves to the archive. On the home screen, tap “Archive” to see your closed groups.
What you can still do in a closed group:
• View all the data and the final summary.
• Record payments (“I paid” / “I received”) for debts that are still open.
• The group organizer can still record an expense. Participants will see the message “The group has been closed for settlement — new expenses go through the group organizer”.
• Anyone joining a closed group joins “From now on only”.
The data is kept in full. The group organizer can reopen it themselves: on the closed group's page, below the message “The group has been closed for settlement”, tap “Reopen the group” and confirm (see “Reopening a closed group”).

articles.title: The app's WhatsApp messages
articles.summary: Ready-made WhatsApp messages: an invite with a link, a personal “My account”, “Who owes whom” and a final summary — you just choose who to send them to.
articles.body:
The app prepares WhatsApp messages ready to send. You just choose who to send them to and tap “Send”:
• Invite — with the group name, who's already in and a join link (from the “Invite” button in the group bar).
• “Send my account on WhatsApp” — at the bottom of the group page: your bottom line and your open transfers.
• Group summary — each participant's account status and who pays whom (from the closing screen).
• Personal closing message — to everyone who still needs to pay, straight to their number (from the closing screen).
Messages are sent from your own WhatsApp. The app doesn't send messages by itself and doesn't read your chats.
In a group with a business license, messages are signed with the business name.

articles.title: Sound and notifications for new expenses
articles.summary: A sound and an on-screen message when someone else records an expense: turning them on and off with the bell or in the settings, and why the browser sometimes asks for permission.
articles.body:
When someone else in the group records an expense, a short sound plays and a message appears on screen. There's no notification for expenses you recorded yourself.
• Turning on or off: the bell button at the top of the group, or “Notifications” in the group settings. The setting is saved on your device.
• When you turn them on, the browser may ask for permission to show notifications. If you allow it, notifications appear even when the app is open in the background.
• To mute just one group, without turning off notifications in your other groups: at the bottom of the group page — “Notifications in this group” → “Don't notify me about every expense in this group” (see “Muting a single group”).
Notifications work as long as the app is open, even in the background. When it's fully closed, no notifications are sent. When you open it again, all the new expenses are already there.

articles.title: “How would you like to receive money?” — Bit, PayBox, bank transfer or cash
articles.summary: “How would you like to receive money?” — Bit, PayBox, bank transfer, cash or PayPal in order of preference, so whoever owes you knows how to pay.
articles.body:
Each participant can say how they'd like to receive money, in order of preference: Bit, PayBox, bank transfer, cash, PayPal or “Other” (with a short note).
Where to set it:
1. When joining — on the “How would you like to receive money? (optional)” row.
2. Or later — on the “Receiving money” row on the group screen or in your personal account.
3. Choose methods, fill in details if needed, and save.
What whoever owes you sees: the methods you chose are shown below their transfer, with copy buttons. The details are also included in the closing messages.
You can tick “Remember these details on this device”, so they're pre-filled in your next group.
The group organizer can set the details for a participant who doesn't have a smartphone. The details will be marked “by…”.

articles.title: Bank account details: who sees them and how they're stored
articles.summary: Bank account details (or IBAN) for transfers: who in the group sees them, how they're stored and encrypted, and what the app checks before saving.
articles.body:
If you prefer to receive a bank transfer, you can enter your bank, branch, account number and account holder name. You can also paste an IBAN, and the fields fill in by themselves.
• The app checks that the account number is valid and warns you about a suspicious number. You can save anyway, but it's worth checking again.
• The account number is shown to group members masked (e.g. •••0022) until they tap “Show”.
• Bank details can be entered only when secure storage is active. Until then, the note “Coming soon” is shown.
• You can change or remove the details at any time. Every change is shown to group members.
• The service doesn't transfer money and doesn't use the details for any other purpose.
Never send bank or card details in a chat — not even to the digital assistant.

articles.title: Alerts about changed payment details — and why it's important to verify
articles.summary: Every change to payment details is shown to group members — a banner, a warning next to the details and a line in messages — so no one can swap details quietly.
articles.body:
So that no one can quietly swap payment details, every change is shown to group members:
• The group page shows a “Payment details updated” banner until you tap “Got it”.
• For the first few days after the change, a warning appears next to the details, and WhatsApp messages include a “Worth verifying” line.
• If your details were changed by someone else (for example, the group organizer), you'll see a message about it too.
What to do before transferring to details that have changed:
1. Call the recipient, or ask them in person, and make sure they really changed them.
2. Only then transfer.
If you didn't make the change to your own details — fix them right away and let the group know.

articles.title: How do participants transfer money to each other?
articles.summary: Money doesn't pass through the app: “Who owes whom” shows who to transfer to and how much, alongside the method the recipient prefers — Bit, PayBox, bank transfer or cash.
articles.body:
Shaveh BeShaveh calculates who pays whom, but the money itself doesn't pass through the app. Transfers are made directly between you — with Bit, PayBox, bank transfer, cash or any method that suits you.
1. “Who owes whom” shows who to transfer to and how much.
2. Below each transfer, the methods the recipient asked to be paid by (Bit, PayBox, bank transfer, cash…) are shown with copy buttons, and they're also included in the closing messages. If the recipient hasn't set a method yet — arrange it with them directly. How to set it: [How would you like to receive money?](article:receive-money-prefs).
3. Transfer.
4. Come back to the app and tap “I paid” next to the transfer (whoever received the money — “I received”).
Tip: Bit and PayBox are two separate apps. Make sure the recipient has the app you're paying with.

articles.title: Plans and prices
articles.summary: Plans and prices: free up to 10 expenses, Week ₪15, Month ₪29, Yearly ₪250 — what each plan includes, top-ups and business licenses.
articles.body:
Group plans (prices are final and include VAT where applicable, and a plan applies to one group):
• Free — up to 10 expenses, with no time limit.
• Week — ₪15: up to 40 expenses, for 7 days.
• Month — ₪29: up to 80 expenses, for 31 days.
• Yearly — ₪250: unlimited expenses, for 365 days.
Top-ups (Week and Month only): 20 more expenses — ₪8; 7 more days — ₪8.
For businesses: Business license — ₪65 a month; Annual professional license — ₪790 a year.
Where to see them: on the home screen, with the “Plans and prices” button — even without a group; and inside a group — in the group settings, “💳 Plans and prices”, which also shows the group's current status and expiry date: [Where do I buy, and what are the prices?](article:where-to-buy).
Only the group organizer chooses a plan. Participants don't pay, unless the organizer decides to split the cost between them.
Groups opened before the price update keep the terms they had. The exact status is shown on the plans screen.
Launch period: when the site shows “Free during the launch period”, all groups have unlimited expenses and there's no need to buy anything — the purchase buttons are disabled and no payment is charged; the prices above are the price list that will take effect when the period ends. For businesses that want their name and logo in their groups — the license card has a “Request a free launch license” button: enter the business name and the phone number you manage your groups with, and the request is emailed to us. Activation is manual, usually within 2 business days. A group opened during this period stays unlimited afterwards too (“Launch-period group”).

articles.title: Where do I buy, and what are the prices?
articles.summary: Where to buy: the “Plans and prices” button on the home screen, or from the group settings — all plans, top-ups and licenses with their prices.
keywords: open a group and choose a plan
articles.body:
The home screen has a “Plans and prices” button — below the group type selection (or your list of groups). It's open to everyone, even before you have a group, and shows all plans and prices:
• Free — up to 10 expenses, with no time limit.
• Week — ₪15: up to 40 expenses, for 7 days.
• Month — ₪29: up to 80 expenses, for 31 days.
• Yearly — ₪250: unlimited expenses, for 365 days.
• Top-ups for Week and Month (from within the group): 20 more expenses — ₪8; 7 more days — ₪8.
• For businesses: Business license — ₪65 a month; Annual professional license — ₪790 a year.
Prices are final and include VAT where applicable.
How to buy:
• A plan for a group — tap “Open a group and choose a plan” next to the plan, choose what you're organizing and fill in the group details. Right after it opens, the group's plans screen opens with the plan you chose selected, and you pay there. In a group that's already open: group settings → “Plans and prices” (for the group organizer).
• A business license — tap “Buy a license” next to the license, even without a group. The license is linked to your phone number and applies to all the groups you open.
How to pay — according to what's shown on screen: “Secure payment” on the site (credit card, Bit, Apple Pay, Google Pay), a payment link, or a ready-made message to the service operator: [How do I pay for a plan or license?](article:how-to-pay).

articles.title: The free plan and what happens when you reach the limit
articles.summary: The free plan: up to 10 expenses with no time limit, what counts toward the limit, and what happens (and what isn't deleted) when you reach it.
articles.body:
Every new group starts on the free plan — up to 10 expenses, with no time limit.
What counts toward the limit: expenses only. Payment records (transfers between participants) and a “Plan cost” expense split between participants don't count.
As you approach the limit, the group organizer sees a message like “3 expenses left on the current plan” with an “Upgrade” button.
When you reach the limit:
• Adding new expenses stops. The plans screen opens for the organizer, and participants get a message that the organizer can upgrade.
• Everything else stays open: viewing, editing, “Who pays whom”, recording payments and closing the group.
During the launch period (when the site and the plans screen say so), the limit doesn't apply — there's no limit on the number of expenses, and a group opened during this period stays unlimited afterwards too.

articles.title: Top-ups: +20 expenses or +7 days
articles.summary: Top-ups for the Week and Month plans, ₪8 each: 20 more expenses while the plan is active, or 7 more days — even after it has expired.
articles.body:
The “Week” and “Month” plans have top-ups at ₪8 each:
• 20 more expenses — available only while the plan is active. They're added to the current plan's limit.
• 7 more days — available both while the plan is active and after it has expired. The days are added from the end of the current validity, or from today if it has already ended.
If the plan has expired, add 7 days first. After that, you can also add 20 expenses.
Where: on the plans screen, in the “Out of expenses or time? Quick top-up” section (or “Plan expired? You can add time”).
The “Yearly” plan has no top-ups, since it has no expense limit.

articles.title: Upgrading a plan by paying the difference
articles.summary: Upgrade a plan by paying only the difference: only plans that give you more are offered, and the price is calculated from what you've already paid.
articles.body:
The plans screen offers only plans that give the group more — more expenses or more time. An “upgrade” that's actually a downgrade is never offered. Next to a plan that your current plan already covers, it says “The group's current plan already includes this”.
The price:
• Switching from a paid plan that's still active — you pay only the difference. For example, from Week (₪15) to Month (₪29): ₪14. The button will read “Upgrade by paying the difference”.
• Switching from an expired plan, from the free plan, or from an older plan that's no longer sold — full price.
The new plan starts from the time it's activated. Top-ups bought for the previous plan don't carry over to it.

articles.title: Renewing a plan
articles.summary: Renewing a plan: the button appears when 7 days or fewer are left, the renewal is added from the end of the current validity — and you don't lose any days.
articles.body:
When 7 days or fewer are left on the plan, or once it has already expired, a “Renew” button appears on the current plan on the plans screen. The same goes for the Yearly plan.
• The renewal is added from the end of the current validity, so you don't lose any days. If it has already expired — from today.
• When renewing the same plan, top-ups you bought are kept.
• The renewal price is the plan's full price.
There's no automatic renewal and no recurring charge. No payment is ever made without you choosing it.
The group organizer sees a reminder on the group page when the plan is about to end, with a “Renew” button.

articles.title: What happens when the plan ends?
articles.summary: When a plan expires: the group returns to the free limit, no data is deleted, and viewing, editing and recording payments keep working.
articles.body:
When a paid plan expires:
• The group returns to the free limit. No data is deleted.
• If the group has fewer expenses than the free limit, you can keep adding up to the limit.
• If it has more — only adding new expenses stops. Viewing, editing, “Who pays whom”, recording payments and closing the group stay open.
• The group organizer sees a message to that effect with a “Renew” button.
To keep recording, you can renew the plan, add 7 days (on the Week and Month plans), or choose a different plan.
In a group covered by a business license: when the license ends, the group returns to the plan it had before.

articles.title: Splitting the plan cost between participants
articles.summary: Split the plan cost between all participants in one tap: the cost is recorded as the organizer's expense and split equally.
articles.body:
Did the group organizer pay for a plan and want everyone to chip in? There's a button for that:
1. Open the plans screen (in the group settings).
2. The “You can split the plan cost between everyone” section shows the amount and the estimate per participant.
3. Tap “Split the cost between all participants” and confirm.
A single expense paid by the group organizer is recorded, and it's split like any other expense. In a “Per head” group — by number of people. This expense doesn't count toward the expense limit.
A double tap or an attempt from another device won't create a duplicate. If the expense is deleted, you can split it again.
This option is shown to the organizer only, and only when the group has more than one participant.

articles.title: Business license and annual professional license
articles.summary: A business license (₪65 a month) and an annual professional license (₪790 a year) for producers, contractors and organizers: unlimited groups, with your business logo and name.
articles.body:
For people who open many groups — producers, contractors and organizers — there are two licenses:
• Business — ₪65 a month.
• Annual professional — ₪790 a year.
What's included:
• Unlimited groups and expenses, in all groups opened by an organizer whose phone number is registered on the license.
• Branding: your business logo and name on invites, in the group header and in messages.
The license is separate from the group's plan and doesn't replace it. When the license ends, each group returns exactly to the plan it had.
Buy it on the home screen — “Plans and prices” → “Buy a license” (even without a group), or from the group's plans screen, in the “For businesses — producers, contractors and organizers” section. There's no automatic renewal.

articles.title: Branding: your business logo and name
articles.summary: Branding with a business license: the logo in the group header, “Courtesy of {business name}” on the invite, a signature on WhatsApp messages and a personal branding link.
articles.body:
While the business license is active, the business's groups are shown under its name:
• The logo appears in the group header instead of the icon.
• The join screen and the invite show “Courtesy of {business name}”.
• WhatsApp messages are signed “{business name} · via Shaveh BeShaveh”.
• A personal branding link shows the app with the business logo and name on the home screen too, on the device it was opened on.
You provide the name and logo when the license is activated. The name and logo appear in groups after a short approval by the service operator — so no one can impersonate another business. A logo with a transparent background stays transparent.
When the license ends or is stopped, the branding is removed automatically and the groups keep working as usual.

articles.title: How do I pay for a plan or license?
articles.summary: How to pay for a plan, top-up or license: from the plans screen, with secure payment or through the service operator — and what happens right after you pay.
articles.body:
Payment for a plan is made from the plans screen:
1. The group organizer opens the group settings → “Plans and prices” (or start on the home screen: “Plans and prices” → “Open a group and choose a plan” — and once the group is open, the plans screen opens with the plan you chose selected).
2. Tap the button next to the plan, top-up or license, for example “Activate by email — ₪29”.
3. A “Before sending the request” screen opens — the item and amount, the business details and the cancellation terms. Tick the Terms confirmation and tap “Send request by email”: a ready-made message to the service operator opens, and all that's left is to send it. The message includes the plan, the amount and the group ID. If your mail app didn't open — “Copy request” and send it to the address shown there.
4. Pay the service operator with Bit or PayBox, following the instructions you'll receive in reply.
5. The plan is activated manually once payment is confirmed — usually within 2 business days — and is shown on the plans screen with its expiry date.
The group keeps working as usual until activation.
When the plans screen shows a “Secure payment” button — you can pay by credit card, Bit, Apple Pay or Google Pay, and the plan is activated immediately: [Secure payment on the site](article:secure-checkout).
A business license can be bought even without a group: on the home screen, “Plans and prices” → “Buy a license”.
You never need to give a credit card number in a message or chat.

articles.title: Secure payment on the site (credit card, Bit, Apple Pay, Google Pay)
articles.summary: Secure payment on the site: credit card, Bit, Apple Pay and Google Pay on Grow's payment page, and what to fill in so your receipt comes out right.
articles.body:
In the web version, you can pay for a plan, top-up or license on a secure payment page:
1. On the plans screen, tap “Secure payment — credit card, Bit, Apple Pay”.
2. Enter your full name (as it will appear on the receipt), mobile phone, and an email for the receipt (optional). For a license, also enter the business name (it will appear in groups after a short approval).
3. Tick the box “I accept the Terms, including the cancellation terms in section 6, and the Privacy Policy”. The box isn't pre-ticked, and without ticking it you can't continue to payment.
4. Tap “Continue to secure payment”. The page of Grow (formerly Meshulam), a licensed payment processor, opens.
5. Pay and return to the app. The app checks the payment with the payment processor, usually within seconds, and the plan is activated immediately.
Your payment method details are given to Grow only and aren't stored by us.
When paying through a Grow payment link (rather than the form on the site), tapping the button opens a short confirmation window: tick the same box there and tap “Continue to payment”. After paying, send us a short message for activation (the button below the link opens it ready-made).
If you see “Payment under review” or “The payment hasn't been approved yet” — there's no need to pay again. The plan will be activated once the payment is approved.
Charged twice or by mistake? Contact us via “Contact a representative” (topic: refund or incorrect charge) or by email at shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com — and the refund will go back to the same payment method.

articles.title: Payment receipt
articles.summary: A receipt for your payment is sent automatically by the payment processor: whose name it's issued in, where it's sent and where to see your purchase details.
articles.body:
When you pay on the secure payment page, a receipt is sent automatically by Grow, the payment processor.
• The receipt is issued in the name you entered on the payment form. So enter your full name, as you'd like it to appear.
• If you entered an email, the receipt is sent there.
• The “Payment received — thank you!” screen shows the amount paid, alongside the “Transaction confirmation”: a document with the business details, what was bought, the price, the period, the right to cancel and how to cancel. You can save it as a file or send it to yourself on WhatsApp.
• Later on too: on the plans screen → “My purchases” → “Transaction confirmation” (for the group organizer). With manual activation — the confirmation is sent to you on WhatsApp.
We store only the transaction details (name, phone, amount and transaction ID) for bookkeeping. Card details aren't stored by us.
Didn't get a receipt? Check your inbox, including spam. If it's still not there — contact us using the details in the Terms.

articles.title: Cancelling a transaction and refunds
articles.summary: Cancelling a transaction and getting a refund under Israel's Consumer Protection Law: within 14 days, how to send a cancellation notice (email or form), and what the cancellation fee is.
articles.body:
You can cancel the purchase of a plan, top-up or license within 14 days of the purchase or of receiving the transaction details in writing — whichever is later, even if the service has already been activated — under Israel's Consumer Protection Law, 5741-1981, and the Terms (section 6).
People with disabilities, senior citizens and new immigrants may cancel within 4 months of the transaction or of receiving the transaction details in writing — whichever is later — when the engagement included a conversation with the service operator (including by electronic communication).
How to give notice of cancellation — any of these ways:
• Using the cancellation form in the app: the “Cancel a transaction” link at the bottom of the home screen, or “Contact a representative” in the Help Center.
• By email: shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com.
• By registered mail — to the address shown on the transaction confirmation.
Service operator: Shimon Stern. Full business details, including the business number and postal address, are shown before every purchase (in the payment sheet, “Business details”) and on the transaction confirmation sent to the buyer.
In your request, include your name, a phone number to call you back and the group or plan name. On the site's form, an ID number is optional — you can include it in your message (a credit card or bank account number — never).
The engagement ends within 3 business days, and the refund — if due — is given within 14 days, minus usage and the cancellation fee set out in the Terms. There's no automatic renewal.
The information here is general and isn't legal advice. The binding wording is the Hebrew Terms.

articles.title: Privacy: what information is stored and who sees it
articles.summary: What information is stored (name, phone, expenses, receipts), why, where (servers in the EU), who sees it and when it's deleted.
articles.body:
What's stored: name, phone number, expense details (amounts, descriptions, dates), uploaded receipt images and group settings.
Why: to show group members the shared account, to identify you when you sign in, to alert you about activity and to activate plans. The information isn't sold or passed on to third parties for marketing.
Measuring where visitors come from: when you arrive from an advertising link (e.g. with utm_source), your browser saves the channel and campaign name in the link and the time you arrived. If a new group is opened from that device within 30 days, the data is saved with the group, so we know which channel brought it. Only the service operator sees it, not group members. No cookies and no third parties. Validity is checked on your next visit, and the record is then deleted from the browser.
Reading from a receipt: when you tap “Read from receipt” in the expense form, the receipt image is sent to the AI provider (Anthropic) to read the amount, currency, date and items only. The provider keeps the image for a limited time only, under its commercial terms (security and abuse prevention), and it isn't used to train models. Without a tap — nothing is sent.
Who sees it:
• Group members — according to the settings the organizer chose. Default: each participant sees only their own.
• The group organizer sees the group's data.
• The service operator — for operations and support only.
• Anyone with the join link can view the group's data.
Where: on Supabase servers in the European Union (Frankfurt), over encrypted connections, and also in your browser's storage on your device.
Full text: “Privacy” at the bottom of the home screen.

articles.title: Deleting data and requests under the Privacy Protection Law
articles.summary: What you can delete yourself — an expense, a receipt or the whole group — and how to request access to, correction or deletion of personal information under Israel's Privacy Protection Law.
articles.body:
What you can delete yourself:
• An expense or a receipt — from within the expense: whoever recorded it and the group organizer delete it directly; other participants send a deletion request for the organizer to approve (see “Deleting an expense and deletion requests”).
• The whole group — the group organizer, at the bottom of the group settings: “Delete group”. The group is permanently deleted, along with all its expenses. There's no way to restore it.
• Information stored in the browser on your device — through your browser settings (clear site data).
Access to, correction or deletion of personal information (under Israel's Privacy Protection Law, including Amendment 13): submit a written request — via “Contact a representative” in the Help Center, by email at shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com, or in any other written way listed in the Privacy Policy. You can view the information in Hebrew, Arabic or English, free of charge. A reply is given within 30 days at most.
Before deleting a group, make sure all debts have been settled.

articles.title: Tips for security and avoiding fraud
articles.summary: Security tips: never send a credit card, code or password in a chat, verify payment details that have changed, and keep your organizer password safe.
articles.body:
• Never send a credit card number, verification code, password or ID number in a chat or on WhatsApp — not even to the digital assistant, and not to anyone presenting themselves as a service representative.
• Before transferring money to details that have changed — verify with the recipient, by phone or in person.
• Send the invite link only to group members. It gives access to the group's data.
• Organizer password: choose a password you don't use anywhere else, and don't share it in the group.
• “I paid” and “I received” are just records. If in doubt, make sure the transfer was actually received.
• Got a message asking for payment “to Shaveh BeShaveh” in a way that isn't shown on the plans screen? Don't pay — check the plans screen in the app first.

articles.title: Accessibility
articles.summary: Shaveh BeShaveh is accessible in line with Israeli Standard 5568 and WCAG 2.1 AA, and has an accessibility menu: larger text, high contrast, highlighted links and more — plus who to contact about an accessibility issue.
articles.body:
Shaveh BeShaveh was built to be accessible to all users, in line with Israeli Standard 5568 and the WCAG 2.1 guidelines at level AA.
What's been implemented:
• Keyboard and screen reader use — buttons, fields and windows are built as components you can operate by keyboard, with screen-reader labels. The known remaining issues, and the date of the last review, are listed in the Accessibility Statement.
• Standard-compliant color contrast, and buttons at least 44 pixels in size.
• A minimum font size of 12 pixels.
• Dark mode — following your device's display setting.
• Forms with clear error messages, and text descriptions for charts.
Accessibility menu: every screen has an accessibility button (the international accessibility symbol) at the top, and the “Accessibility” link at the bottom of the home screen opens it too. In the menu:
• “Text size” — normal, large or extra large; all the text in the app grows, including on buttons.
• “High contrast” — stronger, sharper colors, in light and dark mode.
• “Highlight links” — an underline on every link and an outline on every button.
• “Stop animations” — no motion, transitions or confetti. Turns on by itself when your device is set to reduce motion, and you can change it.
• “Readable font” — a simple, clear font, with wider spacing between letters and words.
• “Line spacing” — more space between lines.
Every change applies immediately. “Reset settings” restores the defaults, and “Full accessibility statement” opens the statement. The settings are saved on this device only — no cookies, no external service and no personal information.
Ran into a difficulty, or finding the digital assistant hard to use? You can get the same service from a person: via “Contact a representative”, by email at shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com, or in any other way listed in the Accessibility Statement. First reply within 2 business days.

articles.title: Adding to the Home Screen on iPhone
articles.summary: Add Shaveh BeShaveh to your iPhone Home Screen: in Safari, tap the Share button and then “Add to Home Screen” — it opens like an app.
articles.body:
You can open Shaveh BeShaveh on your iPhone with one tap, like any app:
1. Open the site in Safari. On iPhone, this works from Safari only.
2. Tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen (a square with an arrow pointing up).
3. Scroll and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
4. Tap “Add”.
The app also suggests this itself, with a “Want it like an app?” banner on the home screen. You can choose “Maybe later”, and the banner won't come back for two weeks.
There's no need for the App Store, and new versions arrive automatically.

articles.title: Adding to the home screen on Android
articles.summary: Adding to the home screen on Android: the “Want it like an app?” banner, or the browser menu → “Add to Home screen”.
articles.body:
1. Open the site in your browser, for example Chrome.
2. If the “Want it like an app?” banner appears on the app's home screen — tap “Add”, and then “Add to home screen” again.
3. Confirm the browser's prompt.
