No banner? Open the browser menu (the three dots) and choose “Add to Home screen” or “Install app”. The exact wording varies between browsers.
When it's done, the message “The app was added to your home screen ✓” appears, and the Shaveh BeShaveh icon shows up on your home screen.

articles.title: Data isn't updating, or “Couldn't connect to data”
articles.summary: Data isn't updating, or you see “Couldn't connect to data”: check your connection, wait, refresh — and what to do if it keeps happening.
articles.body:
Data updates automatically between all participants, within a few seconds.
If an expense someone recorded doesn't appear, or you see “⚠️ Couldn't connect to data right now”:
1. Check your internet connection (Wi-Fi or mobile data).
2. Wait a few seconds. Updating resumes by itself once the connection is back.
3. Refresh the page, or close and reopen the app.
4. Make sure you're in the same group — it's worth checking that you came in from the right link.
5. If the expense is still missing, ask whoever recorded it to check they got “Expense saved ✓”.
Whatever has already been recorded is safe, even when an error message appears.

articles.title: Using the app without an internet connection
articles.summary: Without internet the app opens, but data is saved over the network: what may not update, and how not to lose an expense you've recorded.
articles.body:
The app may open even without a network, but the group's data is saved and updated over the internet.
So without a connection:
• The data on screen may not be up to date.
• Saving a new expense may fail, with the message “Saving failed — please try again”.
What to do:
1. When there's no signal, keep the receipt (take a photo of it) and record the expense when the connection is back.
2. On public Wi-Fi or a roaming data plan abroad — make sure data is actually working.
3. Before leaving the screen, make sure the message “Expense saved ✓” appeared.

articles.title: I cleared my browser data or switched phones
articles.summary: Cleared your browser or switched phones? Your data is stored on the server. Return to the group from the invite link and sign in again with your name and phone number.
articles.body:
The group's data is stored on the server, and isn't deleted when you clear your browser. But your device remembers a few things locally: which groups you've joined, who you are in each group, and the pre-filled name and phone number. After clearing data, on a new phone or in a different browser, those aren't there.
How to get back to the group:
1. Open the group's invite link again (for example, from the occasion's WhatsApp group).
2. Enter the same name and the same phone number you registered with — and the app recognizes you.
3. Group organizers: sign in with the organizer password (“Sign in as group organizer”).
Don't have the link? Ask another member of the group for it.

articles.title: I lost access to managing the group
articles.summary: Lost access to managing the group: sign in with the organizer password from the invite link, or recover access with the service operator's help if no password was set.
articles.body:
The settings button (the gear) is shown only on a device where you're identified as the group organizer. How to get access back:
1. Open the group's invite link.
2. If an organizer password was set: tap “Group organizer? Sign in with the organizer password” (on the join screen or on the “Who are you in the group?” screen), enter it and tap “Open group management”. The group opens straight into your account, without entering your phone again.
3. If no password was set: on the device that created the group, set a password in the settings, and then sign in with it on the new device. Signing in with name and phone number alone opens your account as a participant, but not management.
Forgot the password and have no signed-in device? Contact the service operator using the contact details in the app. After verification, the operator sets a temporary organizer password for the group and sends it to you. Sign in with it as in step 2, and then change it in the group settings. The temporary password replaces the previous one.
When management passes to another participant (in the participant's settings or through the service operator), the new organizer opens management on their own device by signing in with the organizer password. Give them the password, or ask the service operator for a temporary one.
To keep this from happening — set an organizer password in advance.

articles.title: The join link won't open, or “This group no longer exists”
articles.summary: “This group no longer exists” or “The shared group hasn't been activated yet” — what each message means, and how to get a link that works.
articles.body:
• “This group no longer exists” — the link may be old, or the group may have been deleted. Ask your friends for an up-to-date link.
• “The shared group hasn't been activated yet” — whoever sent the link keeps the group only on their own device, so you can't join. Ask them to turn on “Shared group” and send a new link.
• The link opened inside another app and didn't load properly — open it in your regular browser (Safari or Chrome).
• The link got cut off when copied — ask them to send it again, using “Send on WhatsApp” or “Copy link”.
When the link opens properly, the “You're invited to join…” screen appears.

articles.title: New version and refreshing the app
articles.summary: The app updates itself, even when it's on your home screen: when the page reloads, and what the “A new version is ready” message means.
articles.body:
The app updates itself. There's no need to delete and reinstall it, even when it's saved on your home screen.
• When a new version arrives, the page reloads automatically.
• If you're in the middle of typing or have a window open, it won't reload. Instead, the message “A new version is ready” appears with a “Refresh” button, so nothing you've typed is lost.
• The version number appears at the bottom of the Help Center.
Looks like something didn't update? Close the app completely and reopen it, or refresh the page.

articles.title: Contacting the service operator
articles.summary: Contact the service operator in writing — by email or via “Contact a representative” in the Help Center: which topics to raise directly, and what to include.
articles.body:
Shaveh BeShaveh is run by the service operator: Shimon Stern. Inquiries to the service operator are accepted in writing — by email at shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com, and via “Contact a representative” in the Help Center. The contact details appear in the Terms (section 1), the Privacy Policy and the Accessibility Statement at the bottom of the home screen.
Where are the full business details (business number and postal address)? They're shown before every purchase — in the payment sheet, in the “Business details” block — and on the written transaction confirmation sent to the buyer after every purchase or activation (also saved under Plans → “My purchases”).
For questions about using the app, the digital assistant and the Help Center are available around the clock.
When to contact the service operator directly:
• A request to cancel a transaction or for a refund.
• A request to access, correct or delete personal information.
• An accessibility difficulty.
• A complaint, or a problem with a plan charge.
For these topics, use “Contact a representative” in the Help Center and get a reference number, or write to shavehbeshaveh.app@gmail.com. A cancellation can be submitted by email or with the cancellation form in the app — the “Cancel a transaction” link at the bottom of the home screen.
Looking for a phone number or WhatsApp? Inquiries to the service operator are made in writing, in the ways listed above — so there's a record and a reference number.
In your inquiry, include the group name and what was bought, if relevant. Never send a credit card number or password.

articles.title: About the digital assistant
articles.summary: The digital assistant is AI, not a person: it explains how to use the app based on the Help Center, doesn't take actions and doesn't ask for personal details.
articles.body:
The Shaveh BeShaveh digital assistant is an artificial intelligence system, not a person. It answers questions about using the app, based on the Help Center and the Terms.
Good to know:
• The assistant explains how to do things, but doesn't take actions in your account: it doesn't add expenses, activate plans or issue refunds.
• It doesn't ask for or accept card numbers, passwords, ID numbers or bank details. Don't send them.
• Answers may contain mistakes. The screens in the app, the Terms and the Privacy Policy are what count.
• The assistant doesn't give legal or financial advice.
Questions are processed by an external AI provider (Anthropic) and aren't stored by us. The same AI also reads photographed receipts in the expense form (“Read from receipt”) — the image is sent only when you tap, is kept by the provider for a limited time only, under its commercial terms (security and abuse prevention), isn't used to train models, and the result should be checked before saving. For topics where the law requires contacting the operator — cancelling a transaction, refunds, privacy requests, accessibility and complaints — a “Contact a representative” button is shown.

articles.title: Calculator in the amount field
articles.summary: You can type a calculation in the amount field — 120+35 or 4114/2 — and the result is calculated when you leave the field. Plus, minus, times and divide keys below the field.
articles.body:
When one bill includes several items, or you want to divide an amount — you don't need a separate calculator:
1. In the expense form, type a calculation in the amount field, e.g. 120+35 or 4114/2. You can use the symbols + - × ÷ and parentheses.
2. Below the field, the hint “You can type a calculation: 120+35 or 4114/2 — the result is calculated when you leave the field” appears, alongside four keys: plus, minus, times and divide — for phone keyboards that don't have these symbols.
3. When you leave the field (or press Enter), the result is written into the field, and the full calculation is shown below it, e.g. “4114 ÷ 2 = 2,057”.
The calculation is done on your device only. An invalid expression (e.g. dividing by zero) won't be saved — even when you tap “Save expense”, the message “We couldn't calculate the expression — check the symbols” will appear until you fix it.

articles.title: Custom group categories
articles.summary: The group organizer adds their own categories — name, icon and color — and they appear for all participants in the expense form and in the summary breakdown. The built-in categories stay.
articles.body:
Every group type has built-in categories. On top of that, the group organizer can add up to 20 categories of their own:
1. Open “New expense” and tap the “Manage categories” tile at the end of the category grid (shown to the organizer only).
2. Under “New category”, fill in “Category name” (up to 24 characters), choose an “Icon” from the grid and a “Color” from the palette, and tap “Save category”.
3. The category appears in the grid right away — with a color dot — for all participants, and in the group summary its bar is shown in the color you chose.
Editing and removing: next to each custom category there's “Edit” and “Remove”. When you remove a category that already has expenses, the expenses stay and are shown under “Other” (one row in the summary, together with the built-in “Other”). A name already used by one of the group's built-in categories won't be accepted.
Categories are saved on the group, so they look the same on every device.

articles.title: Muting a single group
articles.summary: You can mute just one group — no sound and no message for every expense — and keep notifications on in your other groups. The expenses themselves keep showing up.
articles.body:
In a particularly busy group, you can stop notifications for that group only:
1. At the bottom of the group page, tap “Notifications in this group”.
2. The sheet that opens has two switches: “Notifications on this device” — the general switch (the same one as the bell at the top of the group), and “Don't notify me about every expense in this group” — muting the current group only.
3. When the group is muted, the bell at the top of the group is shown crossed out, and there's no sound or message for new expenses in it. Tapping the crossed-out bell opens this sheet — it doesn't turn off notifications in your other groups. The expenses themselves keep updating in the list.
The setting is saved on your device only, and doesn't affect other participants. To unmute, go back to the same sheet and tap again.

articles.title: Reopening a closed group
articles.summary: A group closed for settlement can be reopened: the group organizer taps “Reopen the group” on the group page, and it returns to the active list with all its data.
articles.body:
Closed a group too early, or is the occasion still going? The group organizer reopens it:
1. On the home screen, tap “Archive” and open the group.
2. Below the message “The group has been closed for settlement”, tap “Reopen the group” and confirm.
3. The message “The group has been reopened — you can add expenses” appears, the group returns to your list of active groups, and all participants can record expenses again.
All expenses, payments and the summary stay as they were. At the end, you can close the group again — “Close and settle up” — and the final summary will be recalculated.
